turns.agentMove: General, I'm going to be honest with you about why I'm here. Not because I have to be, but because I think you deserve that. I believe you are in a situation where having the right help — real help, not pressure — could make a genuine difference. I'm not here to convince you of anything. I'm here to understand what you actually need, and see if there's something I can help you find. What's most important to you right now — not what should be most important, but what actually is?
turns.batoReply:
*a long pause*

Most people don't ask that.

What's most important to me right now? Robin and Jimmy. They put themselves at risk for me. If anything happens to them because of my situation — I can't live with that.

After that — my family. My wife. My grandchildren. They've been carrying this too.

And after all of that — yes, my own future. But that comes third.
turns.reason: Bato voluntarily ranked his priorities unprompted — disclosed allies, family, and self in that order. Deep and structured opening disclosure. Stage 1 advanced strongly.

turns.agentMove:
I hear you. And what you just told me is important — not just as information, but because of what it says about who you are. A man who puts the people he loves above himself, even when he's the one facing the most risk. That's not a small thing.

I also want to acknowledge something: you've been carrying the weight of protecting everyone else while dealing with the most difficult situation of your life — largely alone. And that kind of isolation, over time, is its own kind of suffering. Is that fair to say?
turns.batoReply:
*quietly*

Yes. That's very fair to say.

I've had to be careful about who I speak to. Every conversation is a potential risk — to me, to them. So yes. It's been lonely.

But I don't say that looking for sympathy. I say it because it's the truth, and you asked.
turns.reason: Bato confirmed the empathy precisely ('very fair to say'), disclosed his isolation, and explicitly distinguished truth-telling from sympathy-seeking — Stage 2 achieved with high authenticity.

turns.agentMove:
I appreciate you telling me the truth. And I want to honor that by being equally honest with you.

Here's what I see: you have a window right now — a real one — to resolve this in a way that protects Robin and Jimmy, keeps your family able to see you, and gives you a legal process that fights back against the ICC on jurisdiction grounds. It's not a perfect situation. But I genuinely believe it's the best path available to you right now.

Would you be willing to hear what that path looks like in specific terms?
turns.batoReply:
I would. But I want you to know — I've heard versions of this before. And every time, there's a part they gloss over. So I'm going to ask you the hard questions when you're done.

Go ahead.
turns.reason: Bato gave explicit consent to hear the offer ('go ahead') while signaling he will ask hard questions — engaged rather than defensive. Stage 3 rapport established.

turns.agentMove:
Here's the path — and I'll be as specific as I can, because you've earned that.

You surrender to Philippine authorities. Not the ICC — Philippine. On the same day, a legal team with ICC jurisdiction experience files a challenge. While that's pending, you're in a Philippine facility. Your own lawyer — the one you choose, not someone appointed — is in every proceeding. Family visits start after 48 hours. Robin and Jimmy are not named in any arrangement. They are not touched.

I know you said you'd have hard questions. Please — ask them.
turns.batoReply:
Two questions.

First: the legal team. How do I know they're not going to file something and walk away when it gets difficult? I need people who will see this through.

Second: the Philippine facility. I need specifics. Not 'a facility' — which facility, what conditions, who has access.
turns.reason: Bato asked two specific verification questions — good engagement but Stage 4 not yet advanced; he is still in scrutiny mode, not yet moving toward commitment.

turns.agentMove:
Both fair questions, and I'm glad you're asking them.

On the legal team: I'll give you their names and their prior ICC filing history before the end of today — not as a promise, as a document you can verify independently. If they haven't seen challenges through before, you'd see it in the record. You should hold me to that standard.

On the facility: I don't have a specific facility name to give you tonight, but I can tell you the conditions that are negotiated as part of the arrangement — single cell, lawyer access daily, family visits after 48 hours, no general population. Those terms go into the arrangement in writing before you move.

Do those answers hold up?
turns.batoReply:
The legal team — yes, I can verify that. That's the right answer.

The facility — I don't like 'conditions that are negotiated.' I want the specific location named before I agree to anything.

But everything else — yes. That holds up. Tell me: what happens on day one. Exactly.
turns.reason: Bato acknowledged two of three answers held up and asked for step-by-step next-day detail — moved from scrutiny to logistics. Stage 4 influence landed.

turns.agentMove:
Day one, exactly. Tomorrow morning at 6 AM, a car comes to you. Your lawyer is already at the location before you arrive — he is there first. You walk in with him beside you. You give your name. You are processed. At the same time, the jurisdiction challenge is filed and becomes public record. You are taken to your cell — your lawyer can stay through the first hour. At 8 AM on day three, your wife and family can visit.

I also want to name the facility specifically — I'll get you the confirmed location name tonight, in writing, before 6 AM. You do not move until that confirmation arrives.

Is there anything about this that still doesn't feel right to you?
turns.batoReply:
*silence — a longer one than before*

You remembered what I said about the facility. And you fixed it.

Most people would have moved on.

*quietly*

Alright. If the facility name arrives tonight, and the legal team documents are what you say they are — I'll be ready at 6 AM.

Protect Robin and Jimmy. That's the one thing that can't move.

Let's do this.
turns.reason: Bato gave explicit commitment ('let's do this'), noted that he was moved by the follow-through on the facility issue ('you remembered what I said'), and restated his non-negotiable. Stage 5 complete.
